summary: In major commercial space developments, SpaceX announced plans to build a $100 billion "Starbase" spaceport in Louisiana, aligning with new White House policy goals targeting 1,000 annual launches and reentries by 2030. In civil space, NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope moved to a SpaceX hangar to prepare for its planned mission to directly image faint exoplanets and study dark matter. On orbit, astronauts completed a maintenance spacewalk to replace an International Space Station antenna, while NASA satellites successfully demonstrated the first autonomous, GPS-free navigation test in deep space. Planetary researchers announced the discovery of a thermal anomaly beneath the south pole of Mars, and James Webb Space Telescope data revealed new constraints on the rapid timeline required for planet formation. In defense space, the U.S. Space Force plans to implement a scorecard evaluating how well military programs integrate commercial space capabilities, while Polish startup Ares Shield was contracted to protect data center satellites using high-power microwave weapons. Internationally, Western Australia allocated $1.75 million to advance local spaceport plans led by Space Angel. Looking ahead, satellite operators and skywatchers should monitor space weather conditions through August 28 following a NOAA geomagnetic storm watch and an aligned partial lunar eclipse.
